sections.h2: What should a South Carolina home seller know about the state?
sections.html:
South Carolina has 46 counties, a capital in Columbia and a most populous city in Charleston. Greenville County is the largest county, and sellers deal with county offices for taxes, deeds and many permits.

The 2020 census counted 5,118,425 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 5,570,274. Census QuickFacts shows 71.9 percent owner-occupied housing, a median owner-occupied value of $259,000 and median gross rent of $1,180 for 2020 to 2024. Those are statewide figures, so a house in Greenville, Charleston or a rural county can differ a lot. See the Census QuickFacts page.

sections.h2: How are the regions of South Carolina laid out?
sections.html:
The state splits into the Upstate near the Blue Ridge, the Midlands and Piedmont inland, and the Pee Dee and Lowcountry on the coastal plain.

  • Upstate: Greenville, Spartanburg and Anderson, where the Greenville-Anderson-Greer metro had 975,480 people in 2023.
  • Midlands: Columbia, with a metro of 858,302 in 2023.
  • Lowcountry: Charleston-North Charleston, with 849,417.
  • Grand Strand: Myrtle Beach-Conway-North Myrtle Beach, with 397,478.

The state covers 32,020.5 square miles, about 6.12 percent water. Sassafras Mountain, at 3,560 feet, is the high point, and the coast sits at sea level. Lake Marion is the largest lake at about 110,000 acres. Source: Wikipedia, South Carolina.

sections.h2: What does the economy look like for sellers?
sections.html:
Aerospace, agribusiness, automotive manufacturing and tourism lead, and services make up about 83.7 percent of the economy. Boeing's Charleston facility is the final assembly site for the 787 Dreamliner.

Wikipedia reports a 2025 gross state product of $378.83 billion, an unemployment rate of 4.1 percent in May 2025 and a 2023 median household income of $67,800. A seller in a manufacturing town, a coastal tourist area and a college town will find different buyer pools. Our city guides cover those local differences, and this page sets out the state rules they share.

sections.h2: What should owners know about weather and houses?
sections.html:
South Carolina has a humid subtropical climate, and hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30, with peak risk from early August to early October. Storms that shaped the state include Hazel in 1954, Hugo in 1989, Florence in 2018 and Helene in 2024.

The state also averages about 14 tornadoes a year. For a seller, that means roof age, water intrusion, mold and flood history often come up in a buyer's inspection, particularly near the coast. Sellers of damaged or inherited homes sometimes pick an as-is sale to skip repairs.

sections.h2: How is property tax run in South Carolina?
sections.html:
Counties assess and bill it, and the state sets the assessment ratios and the dates. Under S.C. Code 12-43-220, an owner-occupied legal residence on up to five contiguous acres is assessed at 4 percent of fair market value, and other real property, including commercial, at 6 percent.

PropertyAssessment ratio
Owner-occupied legal residence, up to five acres4 percent
Agricultural, individual or partnership owners4 percent
Agricultural, other corporate owners6 percent
All other real property6 percent
Manufacturer and utility business property10.5 percent

Counties reappraise once every fifth year, and may postpone implementing new values by one year (12-43-217). Taxes are due from September 30 to January 15, with a 3 percent penalty after, plus 7 percent after February 2 and 5 percent after March 17 (12-45-70 and 12-45-180).

Our county and city tax guides cover the local offices. Relief for seniors, disabled owners and blind owners is explained on the SCDOR exemptions page, including the first $50,000 homestead exemption.

sections.h2: How does a deed get recorded in South Carolina?
sections.html:
A deed is recorded with the county register of deeds, or with the clerk of court in counties where that office does the register's work (30-5-10). Before recording, the deed must be acknowledged or proved, and the signing acknowledged in the presence of two witnesses (30-5-30).

Berkeley and Dorchester counties elect registers of deeds for four-year terms. The register records documents in the order they are brought in (30-5-90).

  • Deed recording fee: $1.85 per $500 of value, split $1.30 state and $0.55 county (12-24-10).
  • The grantor generally owes it (12-24-20).
  • An affidavit of value goes in with the deed, and exempt deeds state the exemption reason (12-24-70).
  • Exempt transfers include deeds in lieu of foreclosure, foreclosure deeds to the mortgagee and no-consideration corrective or quitclaim deeds (12-24-40).

sections.h2: What rules apply to rentals, evictions and tenant situations statewide?
sections.html:
Title 27, Chapter 40 sets the landlord and tenant rules for the whole state, and Chapter 37 sets the magistrate court steps. Notice is five days for unpaid rent, 14 days for most other breaches, and 30 days to end a month-to-month tenancy.

The tenant gets ten days to respond to a rule to show cause, and a writ of ejectment follows within five days of a landlord win. Deposits must be accounted for within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Our eviction, tenant rights and homestead guides lay these out in detail.

sections.h2: How do cash sales fit into these state rules?
sections.html:
An as-is sale uses the same recording, tax and deed steps as any sale. What changes is repairs, showings and timing.

A cash buyer can work with inherited homes, properties with tax or tenant questions, and houses with storm or age damage. A closing attorney or title company will still handle the deed, the proration of taxes and the recording fee. Pick the guide for your city or county from the lists above, and ask the local auditor or register of deeds for current figures.

sections.h2: How is the value on a deed figured?
sections.html:
Value means the consideration paid or to be paid in money or money's worth, including forgiveness or assumption of debt, with liens that exist before and remain after the transfer deducted (12-24-30). For transfers between an entity and its owner, or to a trust or beneficiary, value is fair market value.

The affidavit of value must be signed by a responsible person connected to the transaction, and willfully filing a false one is a misdemeanor (12-24-70). Family transfers from a family partnership or trust to a family member, where no consideration changes hands apart from a reduced interest, are exempt, and "family" includes the grantor's spouse, parents, grandparents, siblings, children, stepchildren and grandchildren (12-24-40). Deeds of $100 or less in value are also exempt.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and rules show up in county after county?
sections.html:
The same statewide rules apply in each county even though offices differ. Owner-occupied residential property that receives the special 4 percent ratio is exempt from school operating millage, excluding debt service (12-37-220(B)(47)). Household goods and furniture in the owner's home are exempt from personal property tax.

  • Homestead: first $50,000 of value for owners 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled or legally blind.
  • Refund claims for exemptions must arrive within two years of payment, and rollback taxes reach five preceding tax years (SCDOR).
  • The SCDOR says processing of exemption applications is currently 10 to 12 weeks.
  • If title changes after assessment, the auditor can apportion taxes owed by the original owner (12-45-140).

faqs.q: How many counties are in South Carolina?
faqs.a: South Carolina has 46 counties, and Greenville County is the largest.

faqs.q: When are South Carolina property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due between September 30 and January 15 under S.C. Code 12-45-70. A 3 percent penalty applies after January 15, with more after February 2 and March 17.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in South Carolina?
faqs.a: The county register of deeds does, or the clerk of court in counties where the clerk performs the register's duties (30-5-10). Two witnesses must be present at signing (30-5-30).

faqs.q: What is the deed recording fee?
faqs.a: It is $1.85 per $500 of realty value, made of $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county. The grantor generally pays it.
Yes. A legal residence on up to five contiguous acres is assessed at 4 percent, while other real property is assessed at 6 percent.
